text:
cheng: FYI alert — IAD POP showing ~3x p99 for text-gen routes starting ~10:12 UTC. throughput down ~25% on the same traffic.

sara: seeing it on dashboard too, p50 fine, p95 up ~1.8x, p99 spiking. any recent deploys? :thinking_face:

miguel: no deploys to runtime since last night. IAD kernel-selector logs show repeated fallback decisions around 10:11-10:18.

dana: grabbing profiler + kvcache logs. can someone throw up the network / route graph?

ops-bot: incident created: #INC-2026-18412 (IAD latency spike). Assigned to dana.

cheng: attaching snippets:
```
2026-03-18T10:11:22Z kernel-selector INFO choose_kernel: selected optimized_v2 for model:x, seq=64
2026-03-18T10:11:23Z kernel-selector WARN fallback: high packet loss -> select safe_v1
2026-03-18T10:11:24Z kvcache INFO regen: evicted 14 shards, regen_count=3
2026-03-18T10:11:24Z batching INFO flush_delay increased from 12ms -> 35ms
```

miguel: interesting — kernel selector oscillation with small window. I think it's reacting to network jitter (packet loss) and changing kernels which increases latency and causes kvcache thrash.

sara: network graphs show an upstream provider path change at 10:10:55 UTC, BGP AS path changed for one transit peer. DNS RTTs for our POP spiked, and we saw some TCP retransmits.

anil: CPU steal on one host looks high around same time (procstat shows `steal=22%` on host iad-gpu-12). Could be noisy neighbor + route flap combining.

dana: ran a quick correlation: hosts with high steal also showed more kvcache evictions and longer kernel selection timeouts. probably kernel selector times out waiting on KV responses.

cheng: can we verify kvstore RPC latencies? snippet:
```
kvrpc.latency: p50=1.8ms p95=25ms p99=310ms (hosts with high steal)
kvcache.metrics.evictions: host iad-gpu-12 -> 42 in 5m
```

miguel: that p99 on kvrpc explains regen cascade. kernel-selector measures tail latencies and flips kernels; flipping invalidates caches and increases memory churn — vicious loop.

sara: mitigation idea: pin kernel to `safe_v1` for IAD for next 30m and route a fraction to another POP to reduce load. also cordon noisy host iad-gpu-12.

dana: doing the actions now: 1) apply kernel pin via routing policy (policy_id: rp-iad-pin-safev1) 2) drain iad-gpu-12 3) shift 30% traffic to ORD POP

ops-bot: rollouts: started policy rp-iad-pin-safev1 -> 30% @10:22 UTC

anil: draining host iad-gpu-12 (ssh access) — evicting KVC shards to peers. will take ~90s.

cheng: after pin, p99 came down to ~1.4x baseline and kv evictions decreased. batching flush_delay dropped back to ~14ms. still some DNS jitter but stabilizing.

miguel: root cause hypothesis: upstream provider route flap caused transient packet loss -> increased kvrpc latency -> kernel-selector oscillation -> KV cache evictions -> batching/backpressure -> p99 spike. noisy VM (CPU steal) amplified the latency and slowed recovery.

sara: agree. need two follow-ups: (1) make kernel-selector backoff smarter (avoid rapid flips for transient kvrpc tail spikes), (2) alerting for combined signals (kvrpc.p99 + kvcache.evictions + kernel flips) so we detect the cascade earlier.

dana: filed follow-ups: ENG-PR-1291 (kernel-selector hysteresis/backoff), ENG-PR-1292 (composite alert + dashboard). linking metrics + sample traces in ticket.

ops-bot: incident updated: status=mitigated at 10:34 UTC

cheng: marking as resolved after monitoring window. prepare RCA doc and schedule postmortem review tomorrow 09:30 PT.

sara: add provider contact + watchlist for that transit peer; we should subscribe to their route/maintenance notices.

anil: note: kvcache currently has a safety threshold patch we can enable to avoid full-shard regen for transient RPC spikes — will prototype in ENG-PR-1293.

miguel: thanks all — great triage. leaving the pin for 1 hour and then we'll roll back gradually once metrics stable. :thumbsup:

dana: last checks 10:46 UTC: p99 back to baseline, kvrpc.p99 < 40ms for all hosts. closing thread.
